text: I've said it once before and I will always say it to the day I die, women are always supposed to be the dominant force on this planet. It is embedded in our DNA. It is quite literally coated in us because of the eggs that we possess. I don't know if you know this or not, but the egg is the single largest cell in the human body. The egg decides which sperm gets to procreate. The egg decides it all. Domination starts with us. Male domination is not natural. It never has been and never will be. That's why they have to force it on us. That's why they had to create laws. That's why they had to create religions to put women in their perceived places because they don't like being put in a position that is of submission. For some reason men forgot that that is their natural position. Well, I guess thank you for reminding us. What would we do without you? So your whole argument is that women are natural-born leaders because the human egg cell, which is generally considered the largest single cell in the human body by diameter and volume, is produced in the female body. That is the whole argument? That is the reason? Let's just sit with that for a second. The size of a cell is supposed to tell us who should lead a group of people. Being the biggest cell by volume, that is the proof of leadership? I don't really see how one follows from the other. A thing being large doesn't make it in charge. Otherwise, the blue whale would be running the planet. Quick side note, because I found it kind of funny. The egg cell was only discovered in 1827 by a man actually, the German-Baltic embryologist Karl Ernst von Beyer. So for thousands of years, nobody even knew this cell existed. The code she's talking about was apparently there the whole time, silently running the show. And somehow male-dominated societies kept forming anyway? Make of that what you will. By the way, another fun fact. There is at least some truth in her saying the egg decides which sperm gets to procreate. She really exaggerated it, but it does seem like the egg and the female reproductive tract can favor sperm with certain functional and molecular characteristics. They just cannot precisely choose which individual sperm fertilizes the egg or select specific traits for the future child. Anyways, my whole point is this. There is no credible evidence that one sex is naturally destined to lead while the other is naturally destined to submit. Men and women can both be great leaders. Men and women can both be terrible leaders. Leadership depends far more on the individual person, their abilities, their character, and the situation than on some imaginary social hierarchy derived from the size of a reproductive cell. So how about instead of trying to establish which sex should dominate the other, we simply treat each other with dignity and respect?
